correctness.rationale: The free-space norm is reconstructed exactly as half the \(\ell_1\) mass on the zero-sum hyperplane. The lower bound starts from an arbitrary norm-one operator, uses finite molecular norm attainment, and checks all four sign configurations of the two selected coordinates to obtain a norming indicator with value at least one half. The explicit three-coordinate cyclic operator has norm one on the molecular convex hull, and every norming pair reduces by convex decomposition to normed molecules where its value is at most one half. The two-point boundary is checked separately.

value.rationale: Finite equilateral metrics are the canonical homogeneous finite metrics and coincide with complete-graph shortest-path metrics after scaling. The source literature begins the numerical-index study of Lipschitz-free spaces in dimension two; the theorem turns its equilateral endpoint into a dimension-independent exact law for every finite cardinality, with an explicit extremal operator and a sharp two-point boundary. This is a natural structural family rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
